samples.summary: Merge is scrubbed, but the equivalent "text that was never a heading" path via typing/single-block paste into an emptied bulleted heading is not — the invariant is enforced only for one of the two ways text enters a memory-holding block
samples.evidence: The delta's rationale (docs/design/docs/docs.md:167-190, block-helpers.ts:270-286) is that an emptied bulleted heading which absorbs foreign text must not keep the remembered level, "otherwise removing the list promotes text that was never a heading". The same situation arises without any merge: empty a bulleted Heading 2 (`applyDeleteText` keeps `headingLevel`), then type or single-block-paste body text into it (`insertText` / the single-block paste branch of `TextEditor.paste`, which never touches `headingLevel`). Un-listing then promotes that body text to a Heading 2 exactly as in the merge case. Either both paths should scrub, or the merge scrub is unnecessary and the memory should be treated as sticky-to-the-block (which is also the literal Google Docs behaviour the design doc cites as its parity target — in Google Docs merging a paragraph into an emptied heading yields a heading). As shipped, the outcome depends on invisible state (whether the text arrived by Backspace-merge or by typing), which is a rule users cannot predict.
searchedFor: read TextEditor.paste single-block and multi-block branches (text-editor.ts:3540-3615)
grep mergeBlock / applyMergeBlocks call sites (only MemDocStore + YorkieDocStore implement it)

samples.summary: The heading-memory provenance rules are now split across two layers: `unlistedBlockType` (model/types.ts) restores the memory, `applySplitBlock`/`mergeDropsHeadingMemory` (store/block-helpers.ts) invalidate it
samples.evidence: model/types.ts:331-343 documents itself as the single place keeping the three `toggleList` implementations from drifting, while the complementary invalidation rules live in store/block-helpers.ts:250-294. A future reader looking for "when is the memory valid?" has to find both files; co-locating the predicate with `unlistedBlockType` (or cross-referencing it from the `Block.headingLevel` doc comment, which currently only mentions readers) would keep the rule set in one place. Taste-level; the design doc does tie them together.
